one_line: Paired Kannada scholars of the Hoysala era, one a master grammarian and the other a practical mathematician, embodying the rise of vernacular scholarship.

appearance.age_look: Kesiraja appears mid-40s, lean and composed; Rajaditya appears early-30s, slightly broader-shouldered and energetic.
appearance.face: Both have medium brown complexions; Kesiraja has an oval, thoughtful face with a neatly trimmed short beard, straight nose and calm, perceptive eyes in a mild, analytical half-smile; Rajaditya has a squarer jaw, clean-shaven, lively eyes and a confident, approachable smile.
appearance.hair: Kesiraja’s straight black hair is medium length, oiled and pulled back into a small low knot, with a narrow white cloth band tied around the forehead; Rajaditya’s straight black hair is slightly shorter, also pulled into a low knot, with a thin dark green headband tied above the brow.
appearance.costume: Kesiraja wears a modest Hoysala-period scholar’s outfit: a knee-length off-white cotton tunic (angarkha-style, wrapped left over right) with simple brown edging, over a soft saffron-yellow dhoti folded to ankle length with neatly pleated front; a lightweight pale cream shawl draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around the torso, plus simple brown leather sandals and a single strand of small tulsi-like beads at the neck. Rajaditya wears a courtly yet practical ensemble: a light grey-blue long-sleeved tunic reaching mid-thigh, fastened with a wrap front and dark blue piping, over a deep green dhoti tied to fall to the ankles with a slightly flared hem; a darker green sash (uttariya) diagonally from left shoulder to right hip, used to tuck small tablets, with sturdy brown sandals and a plain copper armlet on the right arm.
appearance.signature: Kesiraja carries a rectangular wooden palm-leaf manuscript bundle of Shabdamanidarpana tied with a red cord in his left hand, while Rajaditya carries a small portable counting board—an oblong wooden tablet marked with etched grid lines and a few dark seed counters resting on it—in his right hand.

ref_desc: Kesiraja and Rajaditya are two medium-brown Hoysala scholars: Kesiraja with off-white tunic, saffron dhoti, cream shawl and red-tied manuscript bundle; Rajaditya with blue-grey tunic, deep green dhoti, green sash and a wooden counting board, both with knotted black hair and sandals.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style model sheet of two Hoysala-era Kannada scholars standing side by side: Kesiraja is lean, mid-40s, medium brown skin, oval thoughtful face with short beard, calm eyes and a mild analytical smile, straight black hair pulled into a low knot with a narrow white forehead band. He wears a knee-length off-white cotton wrap tunic with subtle brown edging, a saffron-yellow ankle-length dhoti with neat front pleats, and a pale cream shawl draped over both shoulders and wrapped once around his torso, plus simple brown leather sandals and a single strand of small beads at his neck; in his left hand he holds a rectangular wooden bundle of palm-leaf manuscripts tied tightly with a red cord. Beside him, Rajaditya is early-30s, medium brown skin, squarer jaw, clean-shaven, lively eyes and a confident friendly smile, straight black hair in a low knot with a thin dark green headband. He wears a light blue-grey long-sleeved wrap tunic reaching mid-thigh with dark blue piping, a deep green ankle-length dhoti with a slightly flared hem, a darker green sash draped diagonally from left shoulder to right hip with small tablets tucked at the waist, a simple copper armlet on his right arm, and sturdy brown sandals; in his right hand he carries an oblong wooden counting board etched with grid lines and a few dark seed counters. Use clear, solid colors—saffron yellow, off-white, green, blue-grey and warm brown—and show them front-facing, full-length, with costumes and props fully visible for consistent redrawing.
